unverifiedSections: NICE NG219 gives no starting dose or maximum; doses are from one undated hospital guideline (UHB same-day emergency care) without page numbers.
The UHB target urate (below 300 micromol/L) differs from NICE (below 360 micromol/L for most people); both are shown.
HLA-B*5801 testing and azathioprine interaction with allopurinol are not mentioned in the sources opened.
No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Rheumatology/Infectious Diseases guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: Urate-lowering therapy is offered for multiple or troublesome flares, chronic kidney disease stages 3 to 5, diuretic therapy, tophi or chronic gouty arthritis. Start at least 2 to 4 weeks after a flare has settled at a low dose and increase using monthly serum urate levels. Allopurinol or febuxostat is first line; allopurinol is first line in major cardiovascular disease. Flare prophylaxis with colchicine is offered when starting or titrating urate-lowering therapy if the person chooses it.

clinicalManagement.title: Offer urate-lowering therapy
actions: Offer for multiple or troublesome flares, CKD 3 to 5, diuretics, tophi or chronic gouty arthritis; discuss with others after a flare.

clinicalManagement.title: Start low
actions: Allopurinol 50 to 100 mg daily; febuxostat 80 mg daily if allopurinol is not suitable and no established ischaemic heart disease or heart failure.

clinicalManagement.title: Titrate to target
actions: Increase allopurinol by 50 to 100 mg until the target urate is reached (maximum 900 mg daily with eGFR above 50); febuxostat 120 mg after 4 to 6 weeks if target not achieved.

clinicalManagement.title: Flare prophylaxis
actions: Offer colchicine; if unsuitable, a low-dose NSAID or low-dose oral corticosteroid, with a proton pump inhibitor where needed; continue 3 to 6 months.

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: Annual serum urate; rheumatology referral if CKD 3b to 5 or treatment fails.

regimens.dose: Start 50 to 100 mg; increase by 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 weeks until target urate; maximum 900 mg daily
regimens.frequency: Once daily (divided doses at higher totals)
adjustments: Maximum by eGFR: above 50 up to 900 mg; 20 to 50 200 to 300 mg; 10 to 20 100 to 200 mg; under 10 100 mg daily or alternate days.
monitoring: Serum urate every 4 to 6 weeks to target, then annually (NICE).
contraindications: HLA-B*5801 testing and interactions are not covered in the sources opened; check product information.
